header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Place Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Ahead for Khilaafah, Are Pleased to Select him and Condemn Anyone who desires to Divide their Unity

blocks.text:
Sa'eed (RA) one afternoon, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) greeted him. Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) said, "Do you want me to pledge my allegiance to you?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "All I want you to do is to enter into the agreement that all the Muslims have entered into." Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) then said, "Let us make an appointment for tonight when I shall pledge my allegiance to you." Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) arrived when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was seated on the pulpit and pledged his allegiance.
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) always had a good opinion of Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed (RA) and respected him. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once dispatched an army to Shaam, he appointed Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) as the commander (and gave him the flag). When Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) took the flag home, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), "How can you give command to Khaalid when he had made those statements in the past?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) insisted so much that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) eventually sent Hadhrat Abu Arwa Dowsi to Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) with the message, "The Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ requests you to return the flag to us." Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) took out the flag and handed it over. He then said, "By Allaah! Just as the appointment to command did not please me, the dismissal does not grieve me. The one to be blamed is someone other than the Khalifah (i.e. Hadhrat Umar (RA))."
Hadhrat Ummu Khaalid narrated further, "It was not long afterwards that Abu Bakr (RA) came to apologise to my father and took a promise from him not to every speak ill of Umar (RA). By Allaah! My father then always prayed for Umar (RA) until he passed away." [^1]
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Marches for Jihaad by Himself and the statement of Hadhrat Ali (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once drew his sword and rode his animal towards Dhu Qassah. Hadhrat Ali (RA) took hold of the animal's reins and said, "Where are you off to, O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ? Today I shall say to you what Rasulullaah ﷺ said to you during the Battle of Uhud; 'Sheath your sword and do not cause me grief (by getting yourself injured or martyred)'. I swear by Allaah that if we suffer any grief through you (coming to harm), Islaam shall never regain its form." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then returned and dispatched an army instead. [^2]
